page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture. It features a single physical Intel Xeon 8163 core supporting hyper-threading to provide 2 virtual CPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a 33 MB L3 cache. It supports instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AES, FMA, and BMI2. The server provides no local ephemeral storage and relies entirely on external network-attached storage, while maintaining a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps under KVM virtualization.

Benchmark measurements place the relative CPU performance of ecs.c5.large in lower tiers. In synthetic evaluations, it recorded a single-core stress-ng CPU score of 1101.79 and a multi-core score of 1461.5. PassMark returned a CPU rating of 1823.49, while Geekbench 6 registered a single-core score of 941.0 and a multi-core score of 1114.0. Uncached memory bandwidth tests measured 10.04 GB/sec for reads and 9.48 GB/sec for writes. Application tests achieved 1.51 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 1.29 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Featuring a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, ecs.c5.large delivers low resource overhead for execution tasks that do not require substantial memory footprints. The absence of local disk drives and modest memory capacity define clear operating limits. The instance is best suited for entry-level microservices, low-traffic static web servers, lightweight utility scripts, and basic background task runners.
